conclusions.claim: Red was simply out-fought in the pivotal R4, taking only 0% of the round's kills (sim-approx: kill share stands in for real trade windows).
Red got the spike down but could not hold it -- only 0% of its plants converted into round wins.
Red was out-traded across the match, taking 44% of round kills over 19 rounds against a 50% even split (sim-approx: kill share stands in for real trade windows).
Blue force-bought in 6 of 19 rounds (32%), past the 30% mark where forcing stops being a read and starts being a habit.
Red was out-spent by Blue by 2245 credits across the match's 19 rounds -- roughly a third of a full team buy in equipment Red never got to bring.
R4 was the match's pivotal round -- the largest single swing (0.252) in the win-probability proxy. Blue took it, Red lost it.
Red reached a plant in only 25% of its attack rounds -- most of those rounds were lost before the spike ever went down.

Red stole 0 of its 1 eco rounds (0%).
